key_insight: The paper extends adversarial robustness certification from risk-neutral RL to risk-sensitive RL by deriving tractable lower bounds on exponential utility under bounded state perturbations.
engineering_relevance: This gives safety-critical RL practitioners a way to certify worst-case performance more realistically when rewards are evaluated with risk aversion, not just expected return.
method: Relax the adversarial state-perturbation set with a c6-divergence formulation.
Convert the certification problem into a convex optimization and derive its dual for a tractable lower-bound approximation.
Decouple training risk aversion (b2) from evaluation risk level to empirically improve certified bounds.
evidence_signal: Experiments on OpenAI Gym tasks and a machine replacement problem show risk-averse training often improves certified lower bounds, especially under larger perturbation budgets, but the trend is non-monotonic.
watch_item: Highly conservative risk-aversion can hurt certification performance, so tuning b2 is important and the best setting may depend on the perturbation budget and evaluation risk level.
paper_title: Certifying Lower Bounds for Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning under Adversarial State Perturbations
